UPCGExClusterSketchCollection.name: Collection | Cluster Sketch
UPCGExClusterSketchCollection.purpose: A collection whose entries are Cluster Sketch assets, so hand-authored clusters distribute with the same weighted machinery as any other staged asset. An entry names a sketch, or flips to a sub-collection of any type; a distribution node picks one per point, and Staging : Load Sketch prints what was picked. A level export fills rows too: a Cluster Sketch component met in a captured level or actor subtree becomes a point on the export's Sketches pin, backed by a row in the shared sketch collection the host maintains, referencing the component's asset or holding an export-owned copy of its inline sketch.
UPCGExClusterSketchCollection.situation: Hand-authored structural pieces have to be picked per point, weighted and categorized like a library of meshes.

mechanism.text: Entries travel the distribute and swap pipeline unmodified through the same type-blind transport as every other collection, so weighted picks, category filtering, collection maps and sub-collection recursion all behave as standard. What is sketch-specific is the staging bounds: a rebuild measures each entry from the sketch model itself, resolving lattice-bound vertices through the sketch's snap provider, with the assets a sketch references loaded first so nested dependencies resolve before measuring. A staged pick therefore fits and justifies like any other asset, with nothing spawnable behind it until Load Sketch prints. An inline row measures its export-owned copy the same way, and Load Sketch prints the copy as it would an asset.

off_label.claim: Sketch entries host inside Omni collections next to meshes, actors and levels: dragging sketch assets into an Omni grid resolves them to this entry type, and a sketch pick that reaches a non-sketch consumer flows past it untouched.
off_label.grounded_in: The editor type registry's DetectSourceAsset routes UPCGExClusterSketch assets to this entry type, and Staging : Load Sketch treats non-sketch picks as expected rather than failed

Entries.semantics: The only type-specific field a hand-authored row exposes is Sketch; entries carry no descriptor block and the collection no type-level globals, because the sketch itself is the whole payload. Source is read-only: a row you add references an asset, and only a level export produces Inline rows, whose copy is not exposed for editing. The copy is not edited in the collection: the component is where the sketch is authored, and re-exporting refreshes the row.

hints.text: A staged sketch pick produces a cluster at execute time, through Staging : Load Sketch; there is no mesh or actor behind the entry.

An inline row is identified by a checksum of its content, the way a mesh row is by its mesh and component settings. Components carrying identical inline sketches collapse into one shared row, and editing a component changes the checksum, so a re-export replaces the row instead of adding one.

UPCGExGetSketchDataSettings.name: Get Sketch Data
UPCGExGetSketchDataSettings.purpose: Reads PCGEx Cluster Sketch components off actors and prints each one as a cluster, placed by the component's world transform, so the output matches 1:1 what is authored and visible in the level. Sketches carrying sites also emit them as plain points on their own pin, ready to seed Find Cells.
UPCGExGetSketchDataSettings.situation: Sketches were authored on actors in the level, and a graph needs them as clusters exactly where they sit.

mechanism.text: Actors are found, their sketch components collected, and each component's sketch in force (inline payload, own asset, or class default) is snapshotted on the game thread so the print runs off-thread against a stable copy. Each snapshot then prints one Vtx / Edges pair through the shared sketch print path, transformed by its component's world transform; the only thing this node adds over the asset's own print is discovery and placement.
steps: Find actors: the shared actor selection, the owning actor by default, or actor references read from the References pin.
Collect their Cluster Sketch components, narrowed by the Component Tags clauses; components PCG itself spawned are skipped by default.
Snapshot each component's sketch and basis on the game thread.
Print one cluster per snapshot, writing authored sketch properties as attributes and the source actor as a @Data attribute.
Print sites as plain points on the Sites pin, independent of whether the cluster itself printed.

off_label.claim: A sketch holding only sites still emits its Sites data, so a component can serve purely as an authored seed cloud with no printable cluster behind it.
off_label.grounded_in: FPCGExClusterSketchPrint prints sites synchronously before the cluster compile and the node stages SiteIOs even when the Vtx output is rolled back with EIOInit::NoInit

Selection.tooltip: Which actors to look for sketch components on. Defaults to the owning actor; Must Overlap Self adds the component bounds to the cache key, so each partitioned cell executes on its own.
Selection.semantics: Ships in Self scope, so a fresh node reads the actor owning the executing component, or the partition actor during a partitioned run, and nothing else. World sweeps the level by class and tag clauses, Parent, Root and Original take one actor from the component, and Include Children extends any of those to the attached actors; the full grammar is on the Actor Selection Details page of the PCGEx book. A selection that can gather nothing warns and stages nothing, and so does a required tag that is also excluded. Must Overlap Self adds the component bounds to the cache key, so each partitioned cell executes on its own. The node subtitle shows the scope, the class and the clauses.

ActorReferenceAttribute.tooltip: Attribute holding the actor reference, read from the References pin. Works on an attribute set or point data alike -- both are read through the same accessor.

ComponentTags.tooltip: Narrows the sketch components on the found actors by their component tags. Blank clauses keep every component.
ComponentTags.semantics: Applied to each found actor's components before the sketch component cast, so a sketch component whose tags fail the clauses is skipped silently; blank clauses keep every component. `Ignore PCGGenerated Components` is folded into the same test, so a sketch component PCG spawned is skipped whatever the clauses say. A required tag that is also excluded warns, since no component can be kept; an entry too long to be a tag warns and stages nothing.

bIgnorePCGGeneratedComponents.tooltip: Skip components PCG itself spawned, mirroring the engine getters.

ActorReferenceAttributeName.tooltip: Name of the '@Data' FSoftObjectPath attribute the source actor is written to.
ActorReferenceAttributeName.semantics: Written on the Vtx data and the site points; the Edges never carry it.

PropertyOutput.tooltip: Which authored sketch properties print, and whether the Map sidecar is emitted.

fields.name: Mode
fields.tooltip: How printed sketch properties are selected.

fields.name: Explicit
fields.tooltip: Explicit selection (and renaming) of the authored properties to print.

fields.name: bOutputMap
fields.tooltip: Also emit the "Map" attribute set of referenced external resources; always on in AllFound mode.

bQuiet.tooltip: Quiet the warnings for actors with no sketch component, and for sketch model issues.
bQuiet.semantics: Changes reporting, never output: the print still emits the valid subset of the sketch either way.

hints.text: Placement is the component's world transform; nothing here targets points. To print sketch assets onto staged points, use Staging : Load Sketch.

A sketch that draws things a cluster cannot represent prints the valid subset: isolated vertices, self-loops, duplicate edges and collocated vertices are dropped with a warning naming the sketch cleanup that fixes them.

UPCGExStagingLoadSketchSettings.name: Staging : Load Sketch
UPCGExStagingLoadSketchSettings.purpose: Prints Cluster Sketch assets onto target points, one cluster per target, inheriting each target's transform. The sketch is resolved per target: from a staged pick through a Collection Map, which is how sketches ride the same weighted distribution as any other staged asset, or from a direct asset reference, constant or per-point. Sites, when the sketch has any, are duplicated per target as plain points on their own pin.
UPCGExStagingLoadSketchSettings.situation: A library of hand-authored pieces has to distribute over points like any other staged asset.

mechanism.text: Each target resolves to a sketch, each distinct sketch is printed once into a shared root cluster, and the root is duplicated onto every target referencing it, so a hundred targets sharing one asset cost one print. Duplicates inherit the target's transform through the Transform Details, and per-target variation comes only from the two Forwarding controls, both of which also apply to the duplicated site points.
steps: Resolve each target's sketch: the staged pick through the Map pin, or the direct reference.
Print each distinct sketch once, deduplicated across all inputs.
Duplicate the root cluster per target, with transform, tags and forwarded attributes applied.
Duplicate the root's site points per target the same way.

off_label.claim: The node can sit inline on a mixed Omni stream and claim only its own entries: a pick that resolves to a mesh or an actor flows past without an error, which is the point of mixed hosting.
off_label.grounded_in: ResolveSketch deliberately does not count non-sketch entries as failures; the header comment names Omni mixed hosting as the reason

A missing staging hash attribute in Collection Map mode is an error in both cases, since it means the targets were never staged with Collection Map output.

fields.tooltip: Attribute name to read from when Input is set to Attribute.

TransformDetails.tooltip: How each printed cluster inherits its target point's transform.
TransformDetails.semantics: The fit is measured once per sketch, on its printed Vtx, and every copy of that sketch places its Vtx, its Edges and its site points through that one box, so the sites keep their drawn place on the cluster however the fit scales or justifies it. A sketch whose cluster does not print is fitted by its own drawn bounds instead, and its sites land in that frame.

TargetsAttributesToClusterTags.tooltip: Which target attributes to promote to tags on the printed clusters.

TargetsForwarding.tooltip: Which target attributes to forward onto the printed Vtx data. A forwarded name equal to an authored sketch attribute REPLACES it on that duplicate -- forwarding recreates the attribute.

fields.name: Matches
fields.tooltip: List of matches that will be checked. Any success is a pass.

fields.name: CommaSeparatedNames
fields.tooltip: A list of names separated by a comma, for easy overrides. The limitation is that they all use the same shared filter mode.

fields.name: CommaSeparatedNameFilter
fields.tooltip: Unique filter mode applied to comma separated names

fields.name: bPreservePCGExData
fields.tooltip: If enabled, PCGEx attributes & tags won't be affected.  Cluster-related nodes rely on these to work!

fields.name: bPreserveAttributesDefaultValue
fields.tooltip: If enabled, will preserve the initial attribute default value.

TargetsForwarding.semantics: Forwarding lands on the Vtx and the duplicated site points alike.
